title: The Paper Letter
premise: In 1917 London, Wendell Yarrow works as driver and courier for a prominent suffragist, quietly reading every letter she carries before delivering it — a habit born of loneliness that becomes dangerous when the letters begin to carry coded anti-war messages. When a census taker named Iris Penhale notices discrepancies in Wendell's household records and starts asking questions, Iris is drawn into the smuggling network herself, torn between her duty to the Crown and her growing love for Wendell. As the armistice approaches, one final letter must reach a dying soldier's family before the ports close, but there is only room in Wendell's last sanctioned convoy for one passenger: Iris's estranged brother, a deserter facing execution, or the suffragist's orphaned niece. Wendell chooses the niece, sacrificing her own chance at escape and trusting Iris to save her brother through official channels; the armistice is signed, the brother is pardoned, and Wendell and Iris build a new family from the pieces war left them.
about_author: Jonah Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in regional record offices. The Paper Letter grew out of a single uncensored envelope found sewn into the lining of a chauffeur's coat.

chapters.title: The Weight of Envelopes
chapters.summary: Wendell Yarrow introduces her routine: driving for suffragist Edith Marlowe by day, steaming open letters by lamplight by night. She tells herself reading is harmless — a way of touching lives she'll never have. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: quiet longing disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Iris Penhale arrives at the Marlowe house and notices Wendell's name appears on no register at all. Her questions are procedural, but her eyes are not. Wendell deflects smoothly, then lies awake replaying the encounter. POV: alternating Wendell/Iris. Emotional beat: first spark of mutual curiosity edged with threat.

chapters.title: What the Steam Reveals
chapters.summary: A batch of letters from soldiers' families contains faint pencil codes between the lines. Wendell realizes Edith is running messages to conscientious objectors' networks. She must decide whether to keep reading or start pretending blindness. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: complicity begins; fear sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Register of Absences
chapters.summary: Iris files her census forms but flags Wendell's blank entry, unable to explain why it bothers her. Reviewing records, she finds three other 'missing persons' all connected to Marlowe's address. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: duty pulling against instinct that something gentler than fraud is happening.

chapters.title: Tea and Interrogation
chapters.summary: Iris returns under pretext of correcting an error. Over tea with Edith, she probes; Edith parries with charm. Wendell watches Iris's hands — steady, ink-stained, honest — and feels seen for the first time in years. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: attraction arriving through suspicion.

chapters.title: Brother, Missing
chapters.summary: Iris reveals, almost despite herself, that her brother Thomas deserted after Passchendaele and has vanished. Wendell recognizes the name from a letter she read weeks ago. She says nothing — yet. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: grief cracking open her official composure.

chapters.title: The Lined Coat
chapters.summary: Wendell finds Thomas's hiding place through the letter's postmark and visits him secretly. He begs her not to tell Iris, believing his sister would report him out of principle. Wendell promises nothing. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the weight of other people's secrets settling onto her shoulders.

chapters.title: Codes and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Edith catches Wendell reading a letter and, instead of anger, recruits her: the network needs someone invisible, someone with clean papers and a driver's freedom. Wendell accepts. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: loneliness transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: Rain on Portland Place
chapters.summary: Wendell and Iris meet again by accident — or not — and walk together through a rainstorm, sharing an umbrella and half-truths. Iris admits she suspects Edith of something criminal; Wendell lets her believe the wrong crime. POV: both. Emotional beat: intimacy built on deliberate misdirection.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Special Branch raids a safe house two steps ahead of the network's schedule. Someone is informing. Edith's courier is arrested; Wendell burns the letter cache in her lodgings' grate, hands shaking. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: terror and the first taste of real consequence.

chapters.title: Suspicions Align
chapters.summary: Iris is questioned about the missing persons file and realizes her superiors suspect Marlowe's whole household. Ordered to report anything irregular, she instead requests reassignment to the file herself — to control what surfaces. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: the moment duty bends.

chapters.title: Confession at the Depot
chapters.summary: Iris confronts Wendell with everything she knows: the false registry, the burned letters, the postmark trail. Wendell confesses all except Thomas's location. Iris, holding arrest power, walks away without using it. POV: both. Emotional beat: love declared through the act of not betraying.

chapters.title: The Informer's Face
chapters.summary: Edith identifies the leak: her own nephew, coerced by threats to his conscription status. The network must move its remaining contacts before he names more. Wendell volunteers for the most dangerous route. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Letters to the Dying
chapters.summary: Among the final letters is one from a soldier at a Kent hospital, asking Edith to tell his mother where he buried a keepsake before he dies. Time matters now; the port closes when the armistice terms finalize. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: urgency giving her errands moral weight.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Edith arranges a last sanctioned convoy — one civilian berth to Dover before the restrictions bite. Three candidates: Iris's brother Thomas, hunted and near capture; the soldier's mother, needed to receive his message; and Edith's orphaned niece, whose guardianship papers require travel. Only one can go. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of mercy.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: Wendell argues each case with herself through a sleepless night: Thomas will hang if caught; the mother will die not knowing; the niece has no one else. Iris, unaware of the choice, asks Wendell directly if she has seen Thomas. Wendell lies to her face for the first time. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: guilt as the price of love.

chapters.title: What Iris Would Do
chapters.summary: Iris discovers the convoy plan and, deducing Thomas is hidden, offers to surrender her claim to the berth — then learns Wendell never intended to give it to him. Fury, betrayal, and understanding collide in a station waiting room. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: love wounded by protection.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Wendell gives the berth to the orphaned niece, reasoning Thomas can be saved only by paper, not passage — by Iris forging a pardon recommendation from inside the system. She sends Iris the evidence: Thomas's service record, his wounds, his letters home. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; trust as a wager.

chapters.title: Forged in Ink
chapters.summary: Iris falsifies the file she was ordered to guard, risking prison to route Thomas into a medical discharge pipeline. The soldier's mother receives her son's letter through Wendell's hand-delivery and finds the keepsake. POV: Iris, closing with Wendell. Emotional beat: two women saving different people the only ways they can.

chapters.title: Eleven O'Clock
chapters.summary: Armistice day. Bells, crowds, strangers kissing in the street — and Wendell arrested on a technicality as the network settles scores. In a cell, she waits, uncertain whether Iris chose the law or her. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: climax; everything staked on another person's courage.

chapters.title: The Last Letter Read
chapters.summary: Iris arrives with Wendell's release — secured by burying the case file beneath Thomas's pardon paperwork. She hands Wendell a letter: her own, written during the worst hours, unsealed so Wendell could read it freely for once. POV: both. Emotional beat: the habit of secrecy broken by invitation.

chapters.title: Household of Four
chapters.summary: Spring 1919: Wendell, Iris, recovered Thomas, and the returned niece share a small house with too many chairs and no empty registers. Wendell still reads letters — but now only ones addressed to her. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: found family complete; memory kept without being carried alone.
